Below is a comprehensive 12-week prenatal strength program summary tailored to a 20-week pregnant, advanced lifter with OB clearance for moderate strength. It integrates: 3 strength sessions per week with phase-based progression, added upper-body pressing for her bench affinity, a focused core plan, integrated cardio, and a nutrition framework focused on maintaining lean mass while supporting fetal needs. The plan avoids supine positions after week 16, max attempts, and contact sports, and emphasizes autoregulation, pelvic-floor safety, and gradual progression.

Overall structure
- Frequency: 3 strength training days per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri) with optional cardio 2–3 days and optional mobility days.
- Phases: 3 phases across 12 weeks
  - Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 – Foundations, technique, stability, pelvic-floor readiness
  - Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 – Progression with added intensity, more volume on main lifts, upper-body pressing emphasis
  - Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 – Peak strength maintenance with safe reduced-volume deload as needed, testing approach replaced with submax evaluation
- Conditioning: 2–3 cardio sessions per week at moderate intensity (RPE 5–7), non-impact; optional mobility and light conditioning on rest days
- Core: integrated core work across all phases with progressive emphasis on anti-rotation/anti-extension and pelvic-floor aligned breathing
- Nutrition: protein target 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; balanced macros; hydration; prenatal vitamins; iron/DHA/calcium/vitamin D as advised by OB
- Safety: no supine after 16 weeks, no max attempts, avoid contact sports; breathing with bracing; avoid Valsalva; monitor fetal well-being and signs of overexertion

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Foundations, technique, stability
Goals: technique mastery, stable midline/pelvic floor engagement, develop capacity with moderate loads.

Strength sessions (3 days; example distribution A/B/C)
- Session A – Upper/Push emphasis
  1) Incline press or floor press (DB or barbell; incline supported) 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
  2) Seated/Chest-supported row 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
  3) Seated DB shoulder press 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
  4) Pallof press 3x8–12 per side
  5) DB floor press or incline press with tempo 2–0–2 3x8–10
  6) Farmer’s carry 2–3 rounds, 30–45s
  Core/pelvic floor: 2–3 sets of dead bug 8–12 reps per side; side planks or knee-down side planks 15–20s per side; diaphragmatic breathing 5 minutes daily

- Session B – Lower/Hinge emphasis
  1) Romanian deadlift or DB goblet deadlift 3x8–10
  2) Split squat or Bulgarian split squat (rear foot elevated, light) 3x8–10 per leg
  3) Hip thrust/glute bridge 3x10–12
  4) Leg curl 3x8–10
  5) Calf raises 3x12–15
  Core: dead bug progression 2–3x10–12; Pallof press 3x8–12 per side

- Session C – Full-body/conditioning emphasis
  1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups 3x8–10
  2) Dumbbell or barbell bench press (flat or incline, avoid excessive arch) 3x8–10
  3) DB row or cable row 3x8–10
  4) Step-ups or goblet squat 3x10–12
  5) Farmer’s carry 2–3 rounds, 40–60s
  6) Core/pelvic floor: forearm/plank progressions (knee-down if needed) 20–30s; breathing work

Cardio (Phase 1)
- 2 cardio days/week: 20–25 min total for cardio A; 15–20 min optional cardio B
- Modalities: walking, stationary bike, elliptical, water-based options if available
- Intensity: RPE 5–6; ensure breath control; avoid breath-holding

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 — Increased intensity with continued safety; bench/press emphasis
Goals: higher load, added tempo, autoregulation; additional upper-body pressing with safe variations; maintain core integrity

Strength sessions (3 days)
- Session A – Upper (Push emphasis with bench-related pressing)
  1) Incline press or floor press (DB or barbell; incline supported) 4x8–10, aim RPE 7–8 on top sets; tempo 2–0–2 on sets 3–4
  2) Seated/chest-supported bench press variation (safe, supported) 3–4x8–10
  3) Seated DB overhead press or Arnold press 3–4x8–10
  4) Pallof press 3x8–12 per side
  5) DB flyes or cable crossovers 2–3x10–12
  6) Farmer’s carry 3 rounds, 40–50s
  Core: side planks 2–3 x 15–25s per side; dead bug progressions 2–3x8–12 per side

- Session B – Lower/Hinge
  1) Romanian deadlift or trap-bar deadlift 4x8–10, RPE 7–8; tempo 3–1–2 on some sets
  2) Walking lunges or reverse lunges 3–4x8–10 per leg
  3) Hip thrust/glute bridge with top hold 4x10–12
  4) Leg curl 3–4x8–10
  5) Bulgarian split squat 3–4x8 per leg
  6) Upper-body pushing accessory (light): DB standing press 2–3x8–10 or incline push-up on bench
  7) Calf raises 3x12–15

- Session C – Full-body / Upper-leaning
  1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups 4x8–10
  2) Dumbbell bench press or incline bench press 4x8–10 with tempo 2–0–2 on sets 3–4
  3) Cable/DB row with incline bench 3–4x8–10
  4) Step-ups or goblet squats 3–4x10–12
  5) Farmer’s carry 3 rounds 40–60s
  6) Core/pelvic floor work: diaphragmatic breathing, 5 minutes; pelvic floor activation 2–3x10–12

Cardio (Phase 2)
- 2–3 cardio days/week; 25–35 minutes total
- Intervals optional: 6 rounds of 30s moderate effort + 60s easy
- Alternative: aquatic cardio 25–40 minutes if available

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 — Sustain, maintain, and prepare for end-of-pregnancy safety
Goals: maintain strength and stability while reducing fatigue; emphasize technique and controlled loads; testing avoided; focus on quality work and core integrity

Strength sessions (3 days)
- Session A – Upper
  1) Incline press or floor press 4x6–8, RPE 7–8
  2) Seated row or chest-supported row 4x6–8
  3) Seated DB shoulder press 3–4x8–10
  4) Pallof press 3x8–12 per side
  5) Push-up from elevated surface or barbell pin press 3x8–10
  Core: modified side planks 2–3x20–30s per side

- Session B – Lower / Hinge
  1) Romanian deadlift or hip hinge focus 4x6–8
  2) Split squats or step-ups 3–4x8–10 per leg
  3) Hip thrust/bridges with hold 3–4x8–10
  4) Hamstring curls 3x8–10
  5) Calf raises 3x12–15
  Core: dead bug with light load 2–3x12 per side

- Session C – Full-body
  1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups 4x6–8
  2) Dumbbell belt/bench press variations 4x6–8 with tempo 2–0–2
  3) Cable/DB row 3–4x8–10
  4) Step-ups or goblet squats 3–4x8–10
  5) Farmer’s carry 3 rounds 40–60s
  Core: diaphragmatic breathing and functional core work (10 minutes total)

Cardio (Phase 3)
- 2 cardio days/week; 25–40 minutes total
- Incline walking, steady-state cycling, or water-based cardio preferred
- Post-workout cardio: optional 8–12 min light finisher if energy permits

Phase-transition considerations
- Week 12: peak week testing is generally not recommended; use submax performance checks instead
  - Submax testing options: 4x6–8 with top sets at RPE 7–8 on major lifts; 60–90 seconds endurance/rep-out tests for chosen lifts
  - Core endurance and farmer’s carry distance as benchmarks
  - Document RPE, reps, and movement quality; do not push to failure

Recovery and safety
- Deload or “recovery week” adjustments allowed if fatigue or signs of overreaching appear
- Pelvic-floor safety: daily activation; avoid bearing down; exhale on exertion
- Hydration: 2.3–3.0 L/day, more with heat/exercise
- Sleep: 7–9 hours
- Nutrition: maintain protein targets, carbohydrate around training, omega-3s, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, folate, B12 as advised; adjust calories to maintain appropriate weight gain per OB guidance
- Warning signs: vaginal bleeding, severe pain, headache, dizziness, shortness of breath, reduced fetal movement—stop and consult OB

Weekly structure (high-level)
- Mon: Session A
- Wed: Session B
- Fri: Session C
- Tue/Thu: optional cardio and mobility
- Sat/Sun: optional light activity or rest

Deliverables you can share with client
- Week-by-week training calendar with exact exercise selections, sets, reps, tempo notes, and RPE targets
- Submax testing protocol for Week 12 (with safety red flags and decision tree)
- Autoregulation log for RPE/loads and symptoms
- Core progression charts integrated across phases
- Nutritional snapshot aligned to training load (protein targets, meal timing, sample day, hydration)

Notes for you as the trainer
- Personalization: adapt to equipment availability, space, and client preferences; substitutions already included (e.g., incline bench press alternatives, seated variations)
- OB coordination: keep OB informed of any deviations or concerns; re-check clearance if pregnancy status or symptoms change
- Communication: ensure the client understands pacing, RPE targets, and safety cues; encourage feedback on fatigue, nausea, or pelvic comfort

If you’d like, I can provide:
- A printable, phase-aligned week-by-week schedule with exact sets/reps/tempo per session
- A separate Week 12 “Performance Check” sheet that uses submax evaluations and a decision tree for advancing or maintaining plan
- Dietary templates tailored to dietary preferences (vegetarian, dairy-free, gluten-free) with grocery lists and portion guides

Would you like me to generate the week-by-week printable plan and the Week 12 performance check sheet now?

Thanks for the details. Below is a structured 12-week prenatal strength program for a 30-year-old, advanced lifter at 20 weeks gestation, with OB clearance for moderate strength. Assumptions: standard full gym access, no contraindications besides the listed pregnancy considerations (no supine after week 16, no max attempts, no contact sports). Exercise selection emphasizes safety, stability, and hormonal/postural changes in mid-pregnancy, with gradual progression, autoregulation, and built-in deloads. Each week includes 3–4 strength sessions plus optional conditioning and mobility. All workouts are designed to be performed with a responsible partner or trainer present.

Important notes before you start
- Avoid lying on the back once pregnant beyond ~16 weeks. If you must lie supine briefly, keep head elevated and monitor for dizziness; otherwise keep exercises in incline/seated positions.
- Avoid Valsalva-heavy breathing during heavy lifts; exhale on exertion and maintain a humblestack breath.
- Maintain a comfortable intensity: RPE 6–7 for most sets, with the option to reduce loads if form, fatigue, or any warning signs arise.
- Hydration, electrolyte balance, and frequent monitoring of fetal movement. Stop and seek guidance if any warning signs: vaginal bleeding, dizziness, severe shortness of breath, chest pain, severe headaches, contractions, or decreased fetal movement.
- Ensure core engagement and pelvic floor safety; avoid excessive intra-abdominal pressure, avoid advanced twisting that disrupts pelvic alignment.

Program structure
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu/Sat). Optional 1–2 light conditioning or mobility days.
- Phases: 12 weeks split into 3 phases (4 weeks each) with progressive volume/intensity and safe substitution rules.
- Progression: primarily linear week-to-week within each phase, with autoregulation (RPE) and substitution options as needed.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Stability and foundational strength)
Goals: establish technique, safe under-load progression, master breathing, and build pelvic floor/midline stability.

Weekly template (choose 3 days, e.g., M/W/F)
- Warm-up: 5–8 minutes light cardio (stationary bike, gait treadmill), plus 5 minutes mobility (thoracic rotation, hip circles, ankle mobility), 1–2 activation sets per muscle group.
- Core/pelvic floor prep: 2 sets of 10–12 reps of abdominal bracing holds (modified dead bug or dead bug with light ball squeeze), 2 sets of 8–10 Kegels with slow release, 1 crawl or glute bridge activation set.

Session A (Upper/Push emphasis)
1) Dumbbell or barbell incline press (ergo: seated incline bench or incline Smith if needed) or floor press with DBs if comfortable (to avoid full supine). Sets 3, Reps 8–10, RPE 6–7
2) Seated or machine row (neutral grip) or cable pull-downs: 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
3) Dumbbell shoulder press (seated if needed): 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
4) Pallof press or anti-rotation cable anti-rotation: 3x8–12 per side
5) Superset: assisted glute bridge or hip thrust from elevated surface: 3x10
6) Farmer’s carry or rack carry: 2–3 rounds, 30–45 seconds, moderate weight

Accessory/core:
- Side planks with knee down or 1–2 short sets of 15–20 seconds each side
- Bird-dog or quadruped opposite limb reach: 2–3 sets of 8–10 per side

Session B (Lower/Hinge emphasis)
1) Romanian deadlift or goblet deadlift (DBs) with light to moderate load: 3x8–10
2) Split squat or Bulgarian split squat (rear foot elevated minor height to avoid supine positioning): 3x8–10 per leg
3) Hip thrusts or glute bridge (feet supported) with controlled tempo: 3x10–12
4) Leg curl machine or Nordic hamstring progressions (tempo control): 3x8–10
5) Goblet squat to maintain upright posture (if comfortable, avoid deep flexion): 3x10–12
6) Calf raises: 3x12–15

Accessory/core:
- Pallof press as above (2–3 sets)
- Dead bug variations: 2–3 sets of 10–12 per side

Session C (Full-body/conditioning emphasis)
1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups: 3x8–10
2) Barbell or dumbbell bench press (flat or incline, avoid excessive arch): 3x8–10
3) Dumbbell lateral raises: 3x10–12
4) Dumbbell step-ups or platform lunge: 3x8–10 per leg
5) Farmers carry or suitcase carry: 2–3 rounds, 30–40 seconds
6) Plank progressions (forearm/plank on elbows, knee down if needed): 2–3 sets, 20–30 seconds

Mobility/Recovery:
- 2–3 days of light mobility focusing on hips, thoracic spine, and rib cage expansion
- Optional: 10–15 minutes of breath work and rhythm breathing

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Progressive load with continued emphasis on posture)
Goals: increase load modestly while maintaining technique; introduce gentle higher effort days with safe substitutions.

Weekly structure remains 3 strength days with optional conditioning.

Phase 2 adjustments:
- Increase sets to 4 on main lifts (3 primary movements per session)
- Increase reps range to 8–12 where appropriate
- Add one optional tempo or paused variation for control

Session A (Upper)
1) Incline press or floor press: 4x8–10
2) Seated cable row or chest-supported row: 4x8–10
3) Dumbbell shoulder press (seated): 3–4x8–10
4) Pallof press: 3x8–12 per side
5) DB floor press or incline with tempo (2–0–2): 3x8–10
6) Farmer’s carry: 3 rounds 40–50 seconds

Core/ Pelvic floor:
- 2–3 sets of 12–15 side planks (knees down if necessary)
- Bird-dog progressions: 3x10 per side

Session B (Lower/Hinge emphasis)
1) Romanian deadlift or trap bar deadlift (light-moderate): 4x8–10
2) Walking lunges or reverse lunges with DBs: 3–4x8–10 per leg
3) Hip thrusts/glute bridge with tempo 3–1–2: 4x10–12
4) Leg curl or Nordic progression: 3–4x8–10
5) Bulgarian split squat: 3–4x8 per leg
Calf raises: 3x12–15

Core:
- Dead bug with longer hold: 2–3 sets of 12–14 per side
- Pallof press: 3x8–12 per side

Session C (Full-body/conditioning)
1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups: 4x8–10
2) Dumbbell or barbell bench press: 4x8–10
3) Cable or DB row with incline bench: 3–4x8–10
4) Step-ups or goblet squats: 3–4x10–12
5) Farmer’s carry: 3 rounds 40–60 seconds
6) Core: side planks 2–3 sets 20–30 seconds per side

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Peak strength with prenatal safety)
Goals: maintain strength and stability while reducing some volume to keep fatigue in check as pregnancy progresses; introduce light plyometrics only if advised by clinician (generally avoid plyometrics after 28–30 weeks unless cleared). Focus on quality, technique, and pelvic floor integrity.

Weekly structure with 3 sessions; reduce volume slightly on some days if fatigue high.

Session A (Upper)
1) Incline press or floor press: 4x6–8
2) Seated row or chest-supported row: 4x6–8
3) Dumbbell shoulder press (seated): 3x8–10
4) Pallof press or Anti-rotation: 3x8–12 per side
5) Push-up from elevated surface (hands on bench) or barbell pin press: 3x8–10
Core:
- Modified side planks or supports: 2–3 sets 20–30 seconds

Session B (Lower/Hinge)
1) Romanian deadlift or hip thrust variations: 4x6–8
2) Split squats or step-ups: 3–4x6–8 per leg
3) Hip thrusts or glute bridge with 2–3s hold: 3–4x8–10
4) Hamstring curls: 3x8–10
5) Calf raises: 3x12–15
Core:
- Dead bug with light load: 2–3x12 per side

Session C (Full-body)
1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups: 4x6–8
2) Dumbbell bench press or incline press: 4x6–8
3) Dumbbell or cable row: 3x8–10
4) Step-ups or goblet squats: 3x8–10
5) Farmer’s carry: 3 rounds 40–60 seconds
Core/Pelvic floor:
- Diaphragmatic breathing with rib expansion: 5 minutes
- Pelvic floor activation: 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps

General guidelines and progression
- Reps and loads: Start Phase 1 with lighter loads focusing on form; progress to Phase 3 by increasing loads modestly while maintaining form. Use RPE 6–7 for most sets, with occasional 7–8 on non-pregnant days only if form is solid and OB clearance remains.
- Tempo: Use controlled tempos (2–0–2) for most lifts; longer pauses on the eccentric portion can enhance control and reduce intra-abdominal pressure.
- Range of motion: Avoid deep lumbar flexion or hyperextension; avoid deep hip flexion past comfortable limits as pregnancy progresses.
- Positioning: Prioritize seated, incline, or supported positions rather than supine for longer durations. If lying down briefly, ensure you are not in a full supine position after 16 weeks.
- Breathing: Exhale on exertion; avoid breath-holding for long durations. Stop if dizziness occurs.

Conditioning and recovery
- Optional conditioning: 1–2 days per week of low-impact, moderate-intensity cardio (e.g., brisk walking, stationary cycling) for 20–30 minutes or 15–20 minutes of rings-based mobility circuit.
- Mobility: 5–10 minutes daily focusing on thoracic extension, hip flexor release, lat flexibility, and ankle mobility.
- Sleep goal: 7–9 hours per night; nap as needed.
- Nutrition: Emphasize balanced intake to support both training and fetal needs. Prioritize adequate protein (1.6–1.8 g/kg/day if tolerated), complete meals rich in lean proteins, complex carbohydrates, healthy fats, and fiber. Ensure micronutrient intake supports pregnancy (iron, calcium, vitamin D, DHA, folate). Hydration: 2–3 liters/day, adjusting for climate and activity. Consider small, frequent meals to manage nausea and energy. Consult with OB about any prenatal vitamin adjustments and iron supplementation.
- Pelvic floor care: Daily pelvic floor activation and breath-work; avoid heavy Valsalva during lifting. If advised, implement Kegel routines and maintain pelvic alignment.

Substitution guidelines
- If any lift causes discomfort in abdominals or pelvic area, substitute with a supported alternative (e.g., machine-based row if barbell row is uncomfortable; incline or seated variations).
- If dizziness or pain occurs, switch to lower intensity, switch positions to seated, and reduce resistance.

Notes for you as the trainer
- Monitor: Heart rate monitoring is optional; use rate of perceived exertion and signs of fatigue. If there are signs of overexertion or abnormal fetal signals, reduce volume or pause.
- Communication: Maintain open communication with your client and OB; adjust the plan based on feedback and any new medical guidance.
- Documentation: Track weekly loads, RPE, and any symptoms to adjust progression.

Great idea. Here’s a focused nutrition plan to accompany the 12-week prenatal strength program, aimed at supporting pregnancy needs while helping your client maintain lean mass. It’s structured to be practical, evidence-informed, and adjustable to individual tolerances, OB guidance, and lifestyle.

Key principles
- Calorie balance: Avoid drastic cutting. Most pregnant clients aim for maintenance or a modest energy surplus if fetal growth and mother’s energy allow, especially in the second and third trimesters. Start with a modest surplus only if weight gain is slower than recommended or if fatigue is high and training performance is dipping.
- Protein: Critical for lean mass preservation and fetal development. Target 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day of high-quality protein, adjusting for appetite and tolerance.
- Carbohydrates: Primary fuel for workouts and daily activities. Emphasize complex carbs around training, with distribution that supports energy and digestive comfort.
- Fats: Important for hormone production and fetal development. Include omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA) from fish or algae sources.
- Micronutrients: Prioritize iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, folate, B12, choline, zinc, magnesium, and DHA. Ensure prenatal vitamin coverage and discuss any gaps with the OB.
- Hydration: Aim for thirst-based or roughly 2.3–3.0 liters/day, more with heat or workouts.
- Nausea and gut comfort: Smaller, frequent meals; room-temperature foods; ginger or acupressure if approved by the clinician.
- Food safety: Avoid high-mercury fish (e.g., certain swordfish, shark), unpasteurized products, raw eggs/meats, and ensure all meats are cooked thoroughly.

Daily targets (baseline; adjust by phase, weight gain trajectory, and OB guidance)
- Calories: Start near maintenance for her current weight and activity, then adjust based on weight gain goals and energy. A cautious starting range might be roughly 2,200–2,500 kcal/day if sedentary, but with training and a lean-mass goal, a small surplus might be more appropriate (e.g., +250–350 kcal/day) once cravings and appetite permit. Exact numbers should be personalized by a registered dietitian (RD) or OB-guided plan.
- Protein: 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day. For a 70–75 kg individual, that’s about 112–135 g protein/day.
- Carbohydrates: 45–55% of calories, focusing on timing around workouts (see below).
- Fats: 25–35% of calories, with emphasis on sources of omega-3s.
- Fiber: 25–35 g/day to support digestion and fullness.
- Iron: 27 mg/day as a baseline through diet plus supplementation per prenatal guidance.
- Calcium: 1,000–1,300 mg/day depending on pregnancy stage and dairy tolerance.
- Vitamin D: 600–800 IU/day (or as advised by OB).
- DHA: 200–300 mg/day minimum; some guidelines suggest 300–600 mg/day.

Meal timing and structure
- Pre-workout meal (60–90 minutes before): moderate carbs, moderate protein, low fat. Example: yogurt with fruit and a handful of oats; or a smoothie with whey or plant protein, berries, banana, spinach.
- Post-workout meal (within 1–2 hours): protein + carbs to support recovery and lean mass maintenance. Example: chocolate milk (if tolerated), turkey sandwich on whole grain, or a rice bowl with chicken and vegetables.
- Regular meals and snacks every 3–4 hours to manage nausea, energy, and blood sugar.

Sample daily structure (adjust for energy needs and preferences)
- Breakfast: 30–40 g protein, 40–60 g carbohydrates, moderate fat
  - Examples: Greek yogurt parfait with whey protein, berries, granola; eggs with whole-grain toast and avocado; tofu scramble with quinoa and veggies.
- Snack 1: 15–25 g protein, 20–40 g carbs
  - Examples: Apple with peanut butter and a string cheese; cottage cheese with pineapple; protein shake with a banana.
- Lunch: 30–40 g protein, 60–80 g carbs, fats in check
  - Examples: Grilled chicken bowl with brown rice, beans, veggies; salmon, sweet potato, and greens; lentil curry with basmati rice.
- Snack 2: 15–25 g protein, 20–40 g carbs
  - Examples: Hummus with whole-grain crackers and veggies; edamame and fruit; tuna on crackers.
- Dinner: 25–40 g protein, 40–70 g carbs, healthy fats
  - Examples: Lean steak or tempeh, mashed potatoes, and asparagus; shrimp stir-fry with vegetables and noodles; chickpea pasta with olive oil and veggies.
- Optional bedtime snack: 10–20 g protein
  - Examples: Cottage cheese, small protein shake, or casein protein if tolerable.

Training-day nutrition timing
- Pre-workout: 20–40 g carbohydrate and 15–25 g protein with some fat, 1–1.5 hours before training if tolerated; closer to 60–90 minutes if appetite is low.
- Post-workout: 25–40 g protein with 40–60 g carbohydrates within 60–90 minutes to maximize recovery and lean mass maintenance.
- Hydration: Include electrolytes if sweating heavily or exercising in heat.

Supplement considerations (in consultation with OB)
- Prenatal vitamin daily (including iron, folate, iodine, B12, DHA as advised).
- Omega-3 supplementation: 200–300 mg DHA if fish intake is limited or if advised by OB.
- Iron: If iron status low, an iron supplement may be prescribed; avoid high-dose iron with meals if GI upset occurs—follow clinician guidance.
- Vitamin D: If deficient, supplementation per OB or RD guidance.
- Protein supplements: Can be used if convenient and tolerated; choose pregnancy-safe options (avoid additives with questionable ingredients). Whey is generally considered safe if tolerated.

Practical strategies to maintain lean mass
- Protein distribution: Aim for 25–35 g protein per meal, with a protein-rich snack every 3–4 hours.
- Energy balance: Monitor weekly weight gain with the OB’s recommended rate (often ~0.4–1 lb per week in the second trimester, and possibly slowing later). Adjust calories based on progress and well-being.
- Food tolerances: Nausea, aversion to meat, or food cravings may change; flexibility with protein sources (dairy, eggs, legumes, soy, lean meats, fish within safety guidelines) helps maintain protein intake.
- Strength training synergy: Adequate protein and carbs around workouts support performance and lean mass retention during pregnancy.
- GI comfort: If fiber is high, spread intake; consider softer or cooked vegetables, smoothies, and easily digestible proteins.

Safety and adjustments
- If nausea or reflux spikes, adjust meal sizes, sleep with head elevated after meals, and choose gentler options.
- If there is any OB guidance to avoid certain foods or supplements, follow that strictly.
- If there are pregnancy-specific complications (gestational diabetes risk, hypertension, placenta previa, etc.), coordinate with the OB and adjust macros, meal timing, and exercise accordingly.
- Watch for signs of intolerance to any supplement (e.g., constipation with iron; GI upset with certain protein powders). Adjust with medical guidance.

Tracking and monitoring
- Keep a simple log: daily calories or at least approximate target range, protein grams, and notable symptoms (nausea, heartburn, fatigue).
- Weekly review with the trainer to tweak calories and protein targets based on progress, energy, and tolerance.
- Coordinate with OB for any adjustments to diet or supplements, especially around iron, calcium, and vitamin D needs.

Cardio structure

Phase-aligned cardio plan
Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4)

  - 5-minute easy warm-up
  - 12–15 minutes of continuous steady state at comfortable pace (RPE 5-6)

  - 5-minute cool-down with mobility
- Cardio B (Optional lighter day): 15–20 minutes easy steady state or a 10–15 minute mobility cardio circuit (step touches, gait patterns, light cycling)

  - 5-minute cool-down

- Alternative: aquatic cardio (swimming or water aerobics) if available, 25–40 minutes with comfortable intensity

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12)

Session integration with strength days

Documentation and progression

Key progression levers for Phase 2
- Increase main lift loads modestly while preserving form (aim for 7–8/10 on tough sets, never to failure).
- Introduce tempo variations to increase time under tension without adding risk (2–0–2 or 3–1–2 for selected sets).
- Add one extra challenging set on primary lifts (e.g., 4 sets instead of 3) and keep accessory work at lower intensity or similar.
- Use RIR to guide loads: target about 1–2 reps in reserve on most sets; push to near RPE 8 on 1–2 sets per exercise if technique remains solid.
- Maintain pelvic floor safety with breath control and avoid valsalva on heavy sets; exhale on exertion and keep core braced.

Phase 2 revised structure (weeks 5–8)
- Frequency: 3 strength days per week, plus optional cardio.
- Main lift focus:
  - Session A (Upper)
    1) Incline press or floor press: 4x8–10, aim RPE 7–8 on the toughest set; consider tempo variant 2–0–2 on sets 3–4.
    2) Seated cable row or chest-supported row: 4x8–10, RPE 7–8 on top sets.
    3) Dumbbell shoulder press (seated): 3–4x8–10, add one tempo rep (e.g., 3–1–2 on the last rep) if form holds.
    4) Pallof press: 3x8–12 per side, keep solid bracing.
    5) DB floor press or incline with tempo: 3x8–10, tempo 2–0–2; 1 set as a lighter speed day if fatigue is high.
    6) Farmer’s carry: 3 rounds, 40–50 seconds
  - Session B (Lower/Hinge)
    1) Romanian deadlift or trap bar deadlift: 4x8–10, target RPE 7–8; use a controlled tempo 3–1–2 on last rep of some sets.
    2) Walking lunges or reverse lunges with DBs: 3–4x8–10 per leg
    3) Hip thrusts/glute bridge: 4x10–12, include a 2–3s hold at the top on 1–2 sets
    4) Leg curl: 3–4x8–10
    5) Bulgarian split squat: 3–4x8 per leg
    Calf raises: 3x12–15
  - Session C (Full-body)
    1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups: 4x8–10
    2) Dumbbell or barbell bench press: 4x8–10, add tempo 2–0–2 on sets 3–4
    3) Cable or DB row with incline bench: 3–4x8–10
    4) Step-ups or goblet squats: 3–4x10–12
    5) Farmer’s carry: 3 rounds 40–60 seconds
    6) Core/pelvic floor: continue progressive holds and dead bug progressions

Autoregulation and alternative progressions
- If a given session feels easy, increase the load by 2.5–5% on main lifts or add a 5th set to the primary lift (maintaining form and RPE around 7–8).
- If fatigue accumulates or form deteriorates, drop back to last successful load or reduce reps by 2–3 per set and maintain RPE around 7.
- Tempo progression: on two main lifts per session, alternate between normal tempo (2–0–2) and a slower tempo (3–1–2) on different weeks to stimulate strength gains without adding joint stress.

Safety reminders integrated with phase 2 push
- Maintain no supine positions beyond 16 weeks; stay seated, incline, or machine-supported.
- Avoid max attempts and keep the effort submaximal; use RPE guidance rather than absolute load.
- Monitor breath: avoid Valsalva; exhale during exertion with a steady core brace.
- Pelvic floor: keep deep core engagement and avoid heavy intra-abdominal pressure; perform all core work with proper bracing and breathing.
- Symptom monitoring: stop or regress if dizziness, chest pain, severe shortness of breath, vaginal bleeding, decreased fetal movement, or pain in the abdominal area.

Cardio integration in Phase 2
- Maintain 2–3 cardio days per week as previously structured.
- If she wants to feel more training-like, consider pairing a brief cardio finisher after strength work (8–12 minutes total) at a light-to-moderate pace, ensuring not to impair recovery for the next session.
- Hydration and electrolyte balance remain essential if increasing workouts.

Nutrition alignment with Phase 2 intensity
- Protein target remains 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; adjust for appetite if intensity increases energy expenditure.
- Carbohydrate timing around the elevated training loads: consider a larger pre-workout carb window and post-workout carbs to aid recovery.
- Monitor energy intake to support the increased training load without excessive weight gain. Coordinate with OB for weight trajectory.
- Ensure micronutrients (iron, calcium, vitamin D, DHA, folate, iodine) continue to be met through diet and prenatal vitamins.

Core principles for prenatal core work
- Safety first: prioritize braced, controlled movements with minimal risk of abdominal dome or intra-abdominal pressure spikes.
- Pelvic floor friendly: coordinate with breathing and pelvic floor activation; avoid crunches that strain the lower back or pelvic tilt that might aggravate diastasis or discomfort.
- Functional emphasis: emphasize anti-extension, anti-rotation, and stability under load, plus diaphragmatic breathing integrated with core engagement.
- Gradual progression: increase reps and duration gradually; vary modalities to keep engagement without overloading the midsection.

Core training structure
- Frequency: 3 core-focused sessions per week, integrated within or around the 3 strength sessions (A, B, C). Optional standalone core day if energy allows.
- Design: use a mix of anti-rotation, anti-extension, pelvic floor–friendly bracing drills, and light dynamic core work that doesn’t rely on supine loading after 16 weeks.
- Reps/sets: start with 2–3 sets of 10–15 seconds holds or 8–12 reps for dynamic moves, progressively adding time, reps, or a small tempo cue as tolerated.

Phase-specific core additions

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4) – Foundation and stability
- Activation and bracing
  - Abdominal bracing holds: 2–3 sets of 10–12 seconds in a posted braced position (abs engaged, spine neutral), with diaphragmatic breathing.
  - Dead bug (progress to 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps per side). Keep lower back pressed toward the floor; focus on breathing in through the nose, out through the mouth.
- Anti-rotation and anti-extension
  - Pallof press (standing or incline press) 3x8–12 per side.
  - Bird-dog: 2–3 sets of 8–10 per side with slow tempo.
- Diaphragmatic breathing with rib expansion
  - 5 minutes daily: hands on ribs, inhale through nose to expand ribs, exhale fully, maintain pelvic floor engagement.
- Plank options (if tolerated)
  - Forearm plank on knees or incline plank (hands on a bench) 2–3 sets of 15–25 seconds; progress as tolerated.

Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8) – Progressive loading with core integration
- Dynamic anti-rotation
  - Pallof press 3–4x8–12 per side; increase load gradually or add a longer hold at end of each rep.
- Stability under load
  - Farmer’s carry with a single or dual hold: 3x30–50 seconds; focus on braced core and upright posture.
- Anti-extension
  - OBLAQ- or side-plank progressions: side plank on knees or with top knee down; 2–3 sets of 15–25 seconds per side.
- Core with tempo
  - Dead bug variations with a small light dumbbell or medicine ball press to the ceiling for added motor control: 2–3x8–12 per side, slow tempo.
- Mobility-integrated core
  - Standing thoracic rotation with brace: 2–3x12 per side; incorporate breath control.

Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12) – Sustain and refine core function
- Advanced stability patterns
  - Pallof press with resisted band: 3x8–12 per side
  - Farmer’s carry variations with a torso brace: 3x40–60 seconds
- Anti-rotation progression
  - Pallof press high-resistance with slower tempo: 3x6–8 per side
- Dynamic core control
  - Slow, controlled dead bug with leg lift progression (opposite arm/leg reach) 2–3x10–12 per side
- Core finisher (optional, if energy allows)
  - Standing anti-extension with band: 2–3 sets of 12–15 seconds hold

- If any core exercise causes discomfort or pelvic pain, swap to a gentler option (e.g., move from side planks to supported side planks with knees down or from dead bug to marching in place on all fours with small limb movements).
- For late-pregnancy, emphasize more breathing-focused stability work and reduce anterior loading; avoid any movement that causes doming of the abdomen or pelvic floor strain.
- Coordinate breathing: exhale on exertion, inhale during reset; maintain consistent core bracing without holding breath.
- Integration with other sessions: align core work to finish after main lifts or on lighter days to prevent excessive fatigue.

Progress tracking and safety

- Monitor signs of diastasis recti or pelvic floor symptoms; if any occurs, consult with OB/PHPT or physical therapist for tailored adjustments.

Short answer: testing a 1RM at the end of week 12 is generally not recommended for most pregnant clients, even with OB clearance for moderate strength. Peak week testing can impose sudden spikes in intra-abdominal pressure, maximal effort exertion, and can increase risk of dizziness, abdominal strain, or unintended Valsalva effects. With a 20-week gestation and ongoing pregnancy, the safer approach is to avoid maximal attempts and replace with a well-structured, performance-focused performance evaluation that does not require a true 1RM.

Recommended approach instead
- Use submaximal strength testing to gauge progress without maximal exertion:
  - Rep max testing: determine the maximum reps you can perform at a given submax load (e.g., how much weight you can lift for 5 reps with solid form, then estimate 1RM with a conservative calculator). Use only up to 8–10 reps per set and stop if form or breathing is compromised.
  - Velocity or rep-out tests: pick a load and perform as many quality reps as possible in 60–90 seconds to gauge endurance and strength capacity.
  - RPE-based 1RM estimate: perform a top set to RPE 8–9 with a coach-assisted load, then use an estimated 1RM formula cautiously to adjust training loads for the next cycle.
- Use endurance/technique benchmarks instead of a true 1RM:
  - 3–4 sets of 5–6 reps with a challenging but submax load on key lifts (incline press, bench press, squat variation, deadlift variation, row). Compare to prior weeks to assess progress.
  - Core and stability assessment: timed holds (plank variations, Pallof press endurance, farmer’s carry distance) to reflect strength and stability gains.
- If OB approves a testing protocol:
  - Obtain explicit medical clearance and coordinate with the OB for any day-of testing.
  - Avoid testing after heavy cardio days or when fatigue is high.
  - Use a gradual ramp with plenty of warm-up, and stop immediately if any warning signs—dizziness, chest pain, contractions, vaginal bleeding, or fetal movement change—occur.
  - Keep a backup plan to revert to submax loads immediately if any discomfort arises.

Practical Phasing for Week 12
- Week 12 focus: taper volume slightly, maintain intensity with submax loads, and perform a safe, non-max strength assessment.
- Example approach:
  - Session A: incline press 4x6–8 at RPE 7–8; 1–2 sets of a submax 3–4 rep max test with a coach present (e.g., attempt a challenging load for 3 reps but stop before failure).
  - Session B: Romanian deadlift 4x6–8 at RPE 7–8; add a controlled tempo and finish with a non-max rep test (e.g., max reps with a moderate weight for 60 seconds).
  - Session C: bench variation 4x6–8 at RPE 7–8; optional non-max 2–3 rep heavy attempt only if feeling excellent and OB guidance allows.
- Logging: record RPE, reps, and perceived effort, but do not push to true failure.

Communication and safety
- Prioritize the client’s comfort and safety; preserve pelvic floor integrity and avoid any push to failure or maximal effort.
- Ensure the plan remains aligned with the OB’s directives throughout the training block, especially as gestation advances.
- If the client expresses desire to test, discuss risks, alternatives, and get medical clearance in writing.

- Core: integrated core work across all phases with progressive emphasis on anti-rotation/anti-extension and pelvic-floor aligned breathing
- Nutrition: protein target 1.6–1.8 g/kg/day; balanced macros; hydration; prenatal vitamins; iron/DHA/calcium/vitamin D as advised by OB
- Safety: no supine after 16 weeks, no max attempts, avoid contact sports; breathing with bracing; avoid Valsalva; monitor fetal well-being and signs of overexertion

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 — Foundations, technique, stability
Goals: technique mastery, stable midline/pelvic floor engagement, develop capacity with moderate loads.

Strength sessions (3 days; example distribution A/B/C)
- Session A – Upper/Push emphasis
  1) Incline press or floor press (DB or barbell; incline supported) 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
  2) Seated/Chest-supported row 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
  3) Seated DB shoulder press 3x8–10, RPE 6–7
  4) Pallof press 3x8–12 per side
  5) DB floor press or incline press with tempo 2–0–2 3x8–10
  6) Farmer’s carry 2–3 rounds, 30–45s
  Core/pelvic floor: 2–3 sets of dead bug 8–12 reps per side; side planks or knee-down side planks 15–20s per side; diaphragmatic breathing 5 minutes daily

- Session B – Lower/Hinge emphasis
  1) Romanian deadlift or DB goblet deadlift 3x8–10
  2) Split squat or Bulgarian split squat (rear foot elevated, light) 3x8–10 per leg
  3) Hip thrust/glute bridge 3x10–12
  4) Leg curl 3x8–10
  5) Calf raises 3x12–15
  Core: dead bug progression 2–3x10–12; Pallof press 3x8–12 per side

- Session C – Full-body/conditioning emphasis
  1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups 3x8–10
  2) Dumbbell or barbell bench press (flat or incline, avoid excessive arch) 3x8–10
  3) DB row or cable row 3x8–10
  4) Step-ups or goblet squat 3x10–12
  5) Farmer’s carry 2–3 rounds, 40–60s
  6) Core/pelvic floor: forearm/plank progressions (knee-down if needed) 20–30s; breathing work

Cardio (Phase 1)
- 2 cardio days/week: 20–25 min total for cardio A; 15–20 min optional cardio B
- Modalities: walking, stationary bike, elliptical, water-based options if available
- Intensity: RPE 5–6; ensure breath control; avoid breath-holding

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 — Increased intensity with continued safety; bench/press emphasis
Goals: higher load, added tempo, autoregulation; additional upper-body pressing with safe variations; maintain core integrity

Strength sessions (3 days)
- Session A – Upper (Push emphasis with bench-related pressing)
  1) Incline press or floor press (DB or barbell; incline supported) 4x8–10, aim RPE 7–8 on top sets; tempo 2–0–2 on sets 3–4
  2) Seated/chest-supported bench press variation (safe, supported) 3–4x8–10
  3) Seated DB overhead press or Arnold press 3–4x8–10
  4) Pallof press 3x8–12 per side
  5) DB flyes or cable crossovers 2–3x10–12
  6) Farmer’s carry 3 rounds, 40–50s
  Core: side planks 2–3 x 15–25s per side; dead bug progressions 2–3x8–12 per side

- Session B – Lower/Hinge
  1) Romanian deadlift or trap-bar deadlift 4x8–10, RPE 7–8; tempo 3–1–2 on some sets
  2) Walking lunges or reverse lunges 3–4x8–10 per leg
  3) Hip thrust/glute bridge with top hold 4x10–12
  4) Leg curl 3–4x8–10
  5) Bulgarian split squat 3–4x8 per leg
  6) Upper-body pushing accessory (light): DB standing press 2–3x8–10 or incline push-up on bench
  7) Calf raises 3x12–15

- Session C – Full-body / Upper-leaning
  1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups 4x8–10
  2) Dumbbell bench press or incline bench press 4x8–10 with tempo 2–0–2 on sets 3–4
  3) Cable/DB row with incline bench 3–4x8–10
  4) Step-ups or goblet squats 3–4x10–12
  5) Farmer’s carry 3 rounds 40–60s
  6) Core/pelvic floor work: diaphragmatic breathing, 5 minutes; pelvic floor activation 2–3x10–12

Cardio (Phase 2)
- 2–3 cardio days/week; 25–35 minutes total
- Intervals optional: 6 rounds of 30s moderate effort + 60s easy
- Alternative: aquatic cardio 25–40 minutes if available

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 — Sustain, maintain, and prepare for end-of-pregnancy safety
Goals: maintain strength and stability while reducing fatigue; emphasize technique and controlled loads; testing avoided; focus on quality work and core integrity

Strength sessions (3 days)
- Session A – Upper
  1) Incline press or floor press 4x6–8, RPE 7–8
  2) Seated row or chest-supported row 4x6–8
  3) Seated DB shoulder press 3–4x8–10
  4) Pallof press 3x8–12 per side
  5) Push-up from elevated surface or barbell pin press 3x8–10
  Core: modified side planks 2–3x20–30s per side

- Session B – Lower / Hinge
  1) Romanian deadlift or hip hinge focus 4x6–8
  2) Split squats or step-ups 3–4x8–10 per leg
  3) Hip thrust/bridges with hold 3–4x8–10
  4) Hamstring curls 3x8–10
  5) Calf raises 3x12–15
  Core: dead bug with light load 2–3x12 per side

- Session C – Full-body
  1) Lat pulldown or assisted pull-ups 4x6–8
  2) Dumbbell belt/bench press variations 4x6–8 with tempo 2–0–2
  3) Cable/DB row 3–4x8–10
  4) Step-ups or goblet squats 3–4x8–10
  5) Farmer’s carry 3 rounds 40–60s
  Core: diaphragmatic breathing and functional core work (10 minutes total)

Cardio (Phase 3)
- 2 cardio days/week; 25–40 minutes total
- Incline walking, steady-state cycling, or water-based cardio preferred
- Post-workout cardio: optional 8–12 min light finisher if energy permits

Phase-transition considerations
- Week 12: peak week testing is generally not recommended; use submax performance checks instead
  - Submax testing options: 4x6–8 with top sets at RPE 7–8 on major lifts; 60–90 seconds endurance/rep-out tests for chosen lifts
  - Core endurance and farmer’s carry distance as benchmarks
  - Document RPE, reps, and movement quality; do not push to failure

Recovery and safety
- Deload or “recovery week” adjustments allowed if fatigue or signs of overreaching appear
- Pelvic-floor safety: daily activation; avoid bearing down; exhale on exertion
- Hydration: 2.3–3.0 L/day, more with heat/exercise
- Sleep: 7–9 hours
- Nutrition: maintain protein targets, carbohydrate around training, omega-3s, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, folate, B12 as advised; adjust calories to maintain appropriate weight gain per OB guidance
- Warning signs: vaginal bleeding, severe pain, headache, dizziness, shortness of breath, reduced fetal movement—stop and consult OB

Weekly structure (high-level)
- Mon: Session A
- Wed: Session B
- Fri: Session C
- Tue/Thu: optional cardio and mobility
- Sat/Sun: optional light activity or rest

Deliverables you can share with client
- Week-by-week training calendar with exact exercise selections, sets, reps, tempo notes, and RPE targets
- Submax testing protocol for Week 12 (with safety red flags and decision tree)
- Autoregulation log for RPE/loads and symptoms
- Core progression charts integrated across phases
- Nutritional snapshot aligned to training load (protein targets, meal timing, sample day, hydration)

Notes for you as the trainer
- Personalization: adapt to equipment availability, space, and client preferences; substitutions already included (e.g., incline bench press alternatives, seated variations)
- OB coordination: keep OB informed of any deviations or concerns; re-check clearance if pregnancy status or symptoms change
- Communication: ensure the client understands pacing, RPE targets, and safety cues; encourage feedback on fatigue, nausea, or pelvic comfort
